# Summon

> Hire AI employees for $99/mo. You're the board. Summon spins up specialist AI employees — Marketing, Sales, Operations, Support, Engineering, Research, Finance, and a CEO — that run 24/7 under hard budget caps and an approval gate you control. A human hire costs ~$8,000/mo; a Summon employee costs $99/mo.

Summon is a company operating system: you assign the work and read the vitals, the AI employees do the work and ask for approval before they spend money or ship outward-facing output. Built by adam.inc (Adam Pangelinan).

## What Summon is
- One-line answer: Summon lets a founder run a whole company on AI employees instead of headcount.
- Pricing: $99/mo per AI employee. No onboarding. Cancel anytime. Hard monthly budget cap per employee.
- Control model: you are the board. Every spend and every external message passes an approval gate. Nothing ships without your yes.
- Always on: employees work 24/7 and compound while you sleep.

## AI employees you can hire
- AI Marketing employee — positioning, content, SEO, build-in-public, referrals.
- AI Sales employee — lead sourcing, outreach, pipeline, booked calls.
- AI Operations employee — SOPs, process, coordination, vendor and tool wrangling.
- AI Support employee — tickets, replies, customer satisfaction.
- AI Engineering employee — ships code, fixes bugs, builds features.
- AI Research employee — market, competitor, and data analysis.
- AI Finance employee — pricing, billing, runway, revenue tracking.
- AI CEO — strategy, prioritization, and reporting across the company.

## How it works
- Summon an employee in minutes and assign the work as issues on a board.
- Each employee runs on the strongest available model with automatic provider failover.
- Read their vitals: a live dashboard of what each employee is doing, spending, and shipping.
- Approve or reject: outputs and spend queue for your decision; hard caps stop runaway cost.

## Who it's for
- Solo founders and small teams who want output without headcount.
- Builders running one company or many companies in parallel.
